facts.text: Sunday Rock, a 64,000‑pound glacial boulder, sits in South Colton and is the only rock listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
In 2009 Sunday Rock was added to the New York State Register, and in 2011 it earned national landmark status.
The Sunday Rock Legacy Project, started in 2012, brings together the Colton Historical Society, the local school, and the Grasse River Players each year.
South Colton, also called Three Falls, lies on NY 56 where the Raquette River crosses, placing it in the heart of the Adirondack Forest Preserve.
Residents like Sally Thomas have long championed Sunday Rock, publishing a booklet titled “Sunday Rock, Its History And The Story Of Its Preservation.”.
The town’s name, South Colton, reflects its position south of the larger Colton town, while the historic hamlet’s nickname “Three Falls” hints at nearby waterfalls.
